objective: Determine whether a preregistered direct test can compare training on uncommon-uncertainty adversarial examples with conventional adversarial training at equal example count and compute.
frozen_question: At equal training-example count and compute, does training on 2004.11573v1 uncommon-uncertainty adversarial examples improve held-out robust accuracy over conventional adversarial training without materially degrading clean accuracy?

sources_and_data.title: Towards Characterizing Adversarial Defects of Deep Learning Software from the Lens of Uncertainty
observations: The paper studies PCS and Bayesian variation ratio (VRO); common benign examples are generally high-PCS/low-VRO (HL), while attack adversarial examples are generally low-PCS/high-VRO (LH).
The paper defines uncommon targets as HH (high PCS/high VRO), LL (low PCS/low VRO), benign LH, and adversarial HL.

For the relevant adversarial HL target, the objective is PCS(x,M) > p, VRO(x,M) < v, and x is an adversarial example; AE(x) is an indicator that the model prediction differs from the benign seed/ground truth condition used by the paper.

KuK generates candidates from a benign seed with random-noise population initialization, an L-infinity constraint, tournament selection, pixel-wise crossover, and white-noise mutation; it iterates until the target is met or computation is exhausted.

Reported settings are population 100, crossover rate 0.5, mutation rate 0.005, L-infinity radius 0.3, 200 benign seeds per dataset, four target types per seed, and at most 50 GA iterations. Reported thresholds are high PCS > 0.7, low PCS < 0.3, high VRO > 0.6, and low VRO < 0.4; the paper says thresholds were selected from prior observed data distributions.

The paper evaluates generated test data against existing defenses; its conclusion explicitly leaves deeper application of uncommon data to robustness enhancement as future work. It does not specify a training intervention, equal-count comparator, equal-compute accounting, or held-out robust-accuracy protocol.

sources_and_data.title: Model Uncertainty project website
sources_and_data.observed: The linked public pages expose paper/results material and figures; no versioned KuK source repository, release archive, commit, dataset manifest, or training implementation was authenticated during this audit.

sources_and_data.title: Guiding the retraining of convolutional neural networks against adversarial inputs
sources_and_data.observed: The dated follow-up uses standard FGSM/BIM/CW examples and uncertainty-guided ordering/configurations (OAR/AR/AF), with an augmented test endpoint. The prior audit records that it does not use the 2004.11573 uncommon generator, does not provide the frozen equal-count/equal-compute comparison, and does not report the prespecified clean-accuracy trade-off.
sources_and_data.evidence_role: near_match_only; not a historical direct label

sources_and_data.observed: The local audit preserves the original source hash and the near-match mismatch assessment. No MNIST/CIFAR10/ImageNet data, KuK code, model checkpoints, or uncertainty-robust training implementation is present in the repository.

method.type: bounded source, provenance, implementation, and local-compute feasibility audit
actions_taken: Inspected the original versioned source and its exact PCS/VRO objectives, fitness functions, GA operators, thresholds, and reported settings.
Inspected the cited project website and searched for a version-pinned public code/data artifact; no authenticated implementation snapshot was found.
Inspected the prior historical-outcome adjudication and kept the 2023 follow-up as a near-match rather than relabeling it.

Checked the current environment: Python 3.9.6; TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch, torchvision, CleverHans, and Foolbox are not installed; nvidia-smi is unavailable; no relevant datasets or code are present locally.
method.not_run: No model training, adversarial generation, proxy experiment, synthetic labels, or hindsight relabeling was performed.

source_intervention_and_comparator.intervention_pinned: Partially at algorithmic definition level: KuK-generated adversarial HL samples satisfying high PCS, low VRO, and AE status.
source_intervention_and_comparator.intervention_not_pinned: No versioned implementation, exact random-noise distribution/seed protocol, full stopping/retry behavior, data preprocessing, or training-label construction is available.
source_intervention_and_comparator.comparator_gap: Conventional adversarial training is not operationally specified by the source. The near-match uses standard attack-generated examples and cannot serve as the comparator definition for this frozen question.
source_intervention_and_comparator.budget_gap: Neither equal training-example count nor equal compute accounting is specified in the source; GA generation cost versus conventional attack-generation cost would also need an a priori accounting rule.

blockers: No authenticated version-pinned KuK code/data/training artifact was found.
The source defines uncommon test-data generation, not the proposed robustness-training intervention or its labels.
Comparator, equal-example budget, equal-compute budget, held-out attack families, and clean/robust endpoint protocol are not source-pinned.
The local machine lacks the legacy Keras 2.2.4/TensorFlow 1.12.0 stack reported by the paper, GPU tooling, and relevant local datasets/models.
observed_result_or_blocker.negative_or_null_preserved: No efficacy result was observed. This no-go is an input/feasibility decision, not evidence that uncommon-uncertainty training is ineffective. The historical near-match remains unadjudicated and is not converted into a positive or negative outcome label.

uncertainty: The paper-level mathematical objectives and headline settings are inspectable, but implementation details needed for exact reproduction are not pinned.
The meaning of AE status during generation and the training-label policy for generated samples would require an explicit new protocol.
A future implementation could make a direct test feasible with new resources; current absence is not evidence that no such implementation exists anywhere.
No sample-size or power calculation is claimed because the intervention and outcome variance inputs are not yet available.

next_falsifiable_action.action: Acquire an author-released or independently archived KuK implementation with commit/hash, environment lockfile, dataset/model manifest, and generation traces; then preregister a matched comparison before running it.
minimum_protocol: Freeze dataset/model/version, seed set, preprocessing, KuK target type and thresholds, generation retries/stopping, and training-label construction.
Define conventional adversarial training and its attack-generation parameters before inspecting outcomes.
Equalize the number of training examples and wall-clock or accelerator-compute budget using the same accounting rule in both arms.

Evaluate clean accuracy and robust accuracy on held-out attack families and held-out generated examples, with independent seeds, clustered uncertainty, and a prespecified material clean-accuracy degradation threshold.
If any required artifact remains unavailable, retain this bounded no-go and do not run a proxy or assign a historical outcome label.
next_falsifiable_action.falsification_gate: The lead fails the proposed benefit if the preregistered uncommon-generator arm has no held-out robust-accuracy advantage or exceeds the prespecified clean-accuracy degradation threshold.
